memories.content: Specify the order and recipients for reporting serious discomfort during the study.
Field staff rely on a pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Establish criteria for halting the use of a design alternative if recurring severe errors appear during formative evaluation.
Do not include a design alternative halted for safety reasons in subsequent evaluation iterations without modification.
Even in controlled environments, delayed prototype recovery procedures increase session interruption time and alter data collection conditions for the same task.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames provide complementary but non-overlapping safeguards. The reference emphasizes incident escalation, unsafe-design controls, and prototype recovery effects; the compared frame addresses burden, accessibility, privacy, equipment, withdrawal protections, and coercion risks. No direct semantic counterpart or scope-aligned disagreement is present.

relations.reason: This incident-reporting protocol appears only in the reference frame, where its specification and staff reliance express one underlying operational claim.
relations.summary: Serious discomfort is handled through a predefined reporting sequence identifying the order and recipients for escalation.

relations.reason: The reference alone specifies the trigger criteria governing when evaluation of an unsafe alternative stops.
relations.summary: Recurring severe errors during formative evaluation require defined criteria for halting a design alternative.

relations.reason: The reference alone governs reuse after a safety halt, a separate lifecycle decision from establishing the initial halt criteria.
relations.summary: A design alternative halted for safety reasons must be modified before inclusion in later evaluation iterations.

relations.reason: This operational consequence of recovery delays appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Delayed prototype recovery increases interruption time and changes data-collection conditions even in controlled environments.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone expresses the task-level burden-to-mitigation mapping and its review control as parts of one policy.
relations.summary: Anticipated participant burden and mitigation strategies must correspond for every field-study task and be verified by the ethics reviewer.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone splits one accommodation-planning requirement into identifying needed access support and describing its delivery.
relations.summary: Necessary accessibility accommodations and how they will be provided must be specified for the field system and research tasks.

relations.reason: This data-handling safeguard appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers must be separated from research data immediately upon collection using a described procedure.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone specifies the inventory decision for participant equipment support.
relations.summary: Equipment available for loan when participants lack necessary gear must be listed.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone addresses the return process, independently from identifying which equipment may be loaned.
relations.summary: The procedure for participants to return loaned equipment must be described.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone states the safe fallback requirement and its role in assessing withdrawal risk as one underlying withdrawal-protection claim.
relations.summary: Field participation requires a safe return to existing work procedures upon withdrawal, because withdrawal risk assessment depends on such an alternative.

relations.reason: This protection against workplace consequences for nonparticipation appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline participation must not be disadvantaged in task assignment or performance evaluation.

relations.reason: This caution about underestimating workplace study burden appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Users may incorrectly infer that a short session entails little burden from work interruption or manager exposure.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers task-specific burden mitigation, accessibility, identifier separation, equipment loans, safe withdrawal procedures, protection from participation penalties, and underestimated workplace interruption and manager-exposure burdens.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers serious-discomfort escalation, safety-based design halting and reuse restrictions, and the effects of delayed prototype recovery on sessions and data conditions.
